title: Greetings
description: Hello and goodbye across the day, with formality notes.

steps.title: A soft start
steps.body: Hindi greetings range from the universal नमस्ते to time-specific forms.

steps.title: Form vs. familiarity
steps.body: नमस्ते works almost everywhere. आप is polite “you”; तुम is informal.
bullets: सुप्रभात = good morning.
शुभ संध्या = good evening.
अलविदा = goodbye.
शुभ रात्रि = good night.

phrases.target: मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। और आप?

Arrange the stones to say: "Hello, how are you?":
steps.explanation: A warm, time-appropriate greeting — the foundation of any first impression.

steps.prompt: You hear this in the morning. What does it mean?

steps.correctAnswer: मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। और आप?
steps.explanation: "मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। और आप?" answers warmly and returns the question with the respectful आप.

title: Please & thank you

steps.body: Hindi interactions expect कृपया and धन्यवाद.

steps.title: Please & thanks
steps.body: कृपया = please. धन्यवाद = thank you.
bullets: बहुत धन्यवाद = thank you very much.
आपका स्वागत है = you’re welcome.
माफ़ कीजिए = excuse me / sorry.

phrases.target: देर होने के लिए माफ़ कीजिए।

steps.body: Family vocabulary combines with "to have" and possessives for quick descriptions.

steps.title: Possessives and gender
steps.body: Possessives work differently in each language.
bullets: Portuguese: meu/minha agree with the noun
Arabic: possessive suffixes attach to the noun
Hindi: मेरा/मेरी agree with the noun gender

phrases.target: मेरे माता-पिता दिल्ली में रहते हैं.

steps.title: Listen · possessive
steps.prompt: How do you say "my sister" in Hindi?

steps.partnerSays: मिलकर बहुत खुशी हुई। क्या आपके भाई-बहन हैं?
steps.partnerSaysTranslation: Nice to meet you. Do you have siblings?
steps.partnerSaysPhonetic: Milkar bahut khushī huī. Kyā āpke bhāī-bahan haiṅ?
steps.prompt: Say you have two brothers:
steps.explanation: "हाँ, मेरे दो भाई हैं" answers directly.

steps.title: Check · possessive
steps.prompt: How do you say "my sister" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: बहन is feminine → मेरी बहन. मेरा is masculine, मेरी is feminine.

steps.title: Check · plural
steps.prompt: How do you say "my parents" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: माता-पिता is plural → मेरे माता-पिता (plural possessive form).

title: Shopping for clothes
description: Sizes, trying things on, and asking about price.

steps.title: Trying it on
steps.body: Clothes shopping mixes size, color, and a few polite requests to try things on or ask for a different size.

phrases.source: Do you have this in a size 40?
phrases.target: क्या यह साइज़ चालीस में है?
क्या मैं इसे पहन कर देख सकता हूँ?

phrases.source: Do you have a bigger size?

steps.targetTranslation: Do you have this in a size 40?
steps.explanation: The one question that keeps a shopping trip moving in the right direction.

steps.title: Listen · size
steps.prompt: How do you say "It's too small"?

steps.partnerSaysTranslation: Of course. The fitting room is over there.
steps.prompt: After trying it on, say it's too small and ask for a bigger size:

steps.correctAnswer: यह बहुत छोटा है। क्या इससे बड़ा साइज़ है?
steps.explanation: "यह बहुत छोटा है। क्या इससे बड़ा साइज़ है?" describes the problem and asks for the next size.

steps.title: Check · size
steps.prompt: How do you ask "do you have this in size 40?"
options: क्या यह साइज़ चालीस में है?
steps.explanation: साइज़ means size; साइज़ चालीस में = in size 40.

steps.title: Check · too small
steps.prompt: How do you say "It's too small" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: बहुत छोटा = too small; बहुत बड़ा = too big.

title: Articles & gender
description: Noun gender and grammatical articles (or their equivalents).

steps.title: Nouns and their markers
steps.body: Portuguese has gender like French; Arabic has gender but a single definite article; Hindi has gender with no articles at all.

steps.title: Key differences
steps.body: Each language handles definiteness and gender differently.
bullets: Portuguese: o/a (the), um/uma (a) — 2 genders
Arabic: الـ (al-) for all definite nouns — 2 genders
Hindi: no articles; gender affects adjectives and verb agreement

steps.prompt: Match each Hindi word with its English meaning:
Arrange the stones to say: "The table is good.":
steps.explanation: A compact phrase that puts the article or gender rule into immediate practice.

steps.title: Listen · gender agreement
steps.prompt: Which adjective form matches "बहन" (sister, feminine)?
steps.explanation: बहन is feminine → the feminine adjective form अच्छी.

steps.partnerSays: हिंदी में "table" का लिंग क्या है?
steps.partnerSaysTranslation: What is the gender of "table" in Hindi?
steps.partnerSaysPhonetic: Hindī meṅ "table" kā liṅg kyā hai?
steps.prompt: Answer correctly:
steps.explanation: मेज़ (table) is feminine (स्त्रीलिंग) in Hindi. Gender affects verb and adjective forms.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: मेज़ (table) is which gender in Hindi?
steps.explanation: मेज़ is feminine (स्त्रीलिंग). This affects adjective forms and verb agreement.

steps.title: Check · agreement
steps.prompt: How do you say "The boy is good" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: लड़का is masculine → अच्छा (masculine adjective).

steps.title: Check · articles
steps.prompt: Which statement about Hindi articles is correct?
steps.explanation: Hindi has no articles. Definiteness is shown by context or demonstratives (यह, वह).

title: To be & to have
description: The two verbs you'll use every day.

steps.title: Workhorses
steps.body: The verbs "to be" and "to have" appear constantly in descriptions, states, and idioms.

items.meaning: उनके पास है / उसके पास है

phrases.note: Idiom: भूख लगना = to feel hungry

steps.prompt: Match each Hindi word with its English meaning:
Arrange the stones to say: "I am tired.":
steps.explanation: Two core verbs in a single sentence — a powerful combination to internalize.

steps.title: Listen · idiom
steps.prompt: How do you say "They are hungry"?
Say you're tired and hungry:
options: मैं थका हुआ हूँ और मुझे भूख लगी है.
मैं भूखा हूँ और थका लगती है.
थका हुआ और भूख लगती है.
steps.correctAnswer: मैं थका हुआ हूँ और मुझे भूख लगी है.
steps.explanation: Tiredness uses हूँ (am), while hunger uses मुझे लगी है (I feel/have).

steps.title: Check · to be
steps.prompt: How do you say "I am" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: मैं हूँ = I am. हूँ is the first person singular form of होना (to be).

steps.title: Check · to have
steps.prompt: "मेरे पास बुकिंग है" means…
steps.explanation: मेरे पास = at/with me = I have; बुकिंग है = there is a booking.

steps.title: Check · idiom
steps.prompt: How do you say "they are hungry" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: भूख लगना is the idiom — Hindi uses "feel hunger" where English uses "be hungry".

title: Regular verbs
description: Conjugate the most common verb family.

steps.title: The biggest group
steps.body: Most verbs follow a regular pattern — learn it once, apply it to hundreds of verbs.

steps.title: Patterns compared
steps.body: Each language has its main verb conjugation pattern.
bullets: Portuguese: -ar verbs (falar) → falo, falas, fala, falamos, falam
Arabic: present tense uses prefix + suffix patterns: أتكلم، تتكلم، يتكلم
Hindi: verb + gender/number + tense marker: बोलता हूँ (m.), बोलती हूँ (f.)

phrases.target: हम दिल्ली में काम करते हैं.
वह भारतीय खाना पसंद करती है.

steps.prompt: Match each Hindi word with its English meaning:
Arrange the stones to say: "I speak a little Hindi.":
steps.explanation: The verb pattern in action — master this form and unlock a whole verb family.

steps.title: Listen · she form
steps.prompt: Which form is correct for "she speaks"?
Say yes, you speak a little Hindi:
options: हाँ, तुम थोड़ी हिंदी बोलता हूँ.
हाँ, हम थोड़ी हिंदी बोलता हूँ.
steps.explanation: With मैं, the verb form for masculine is बोलता हूँ. For feminine: बोलती हूँ.

steps.title: Check · gender
steps.prompt: What form of "speak" does a woman use for "I speak"?
steps.explanation: बोलती हूँ is the feminine first person singular: मैं बोलती हूँ.

steps.title: Check · she
steps.prompt: What form means "she speaks"?
steps.explanation: She is feminine → वह बोलती है.

title: Adjective agreement
description: Make descriptive words match the noun they describe.

steps.title: Adjectives match their nouns
steps.body: Portuguese adjectives agree with gender/number. Arabic adjectives agree with gender, number, and definiteness. Hindi adjectives agree with gender and number.

steps.title: The default rule
steps.body: Add -a/-e for feminine in Portuguese; change the ending in Arabic; change -ā to -ī in Hindi.
bullets: Portuguese: alto → alta (f.), altos (m. pl.), altas (f. pl.)
Arabic: طويل (m.) → طويلة (f.)
Hindi: लंबा (m.) → लंबी (f.) → लंबे (m. pl.)

steps.prompt: Match each Hindi word with its English meaning:
Arrange the stones to say: "She is small.":
steps.explanation: Agreement at work: the adjective shifts to match the noun it describes.

steps.title: Listen · feminine
steps.prompt: Which adjective form goes with "बहन" (sister, feminine)?

steps.partnerSays: मेरा भाई लंबा है। और तुम्हारी बहन?
steps.partnerSaysTranslation: My brother is tall. And your sister?
steps.partnerSaysPhonetic: Merā bhāī lambā hai. Aur tumhārī bahan?
steps.prompt: Describe your sister the same way:
steps.explanation: Hindi adjectives agree with gender: लंबा (masc.) becomes लंबी (fem.) for बहन.

steps.title: Check · feminine
steps.prompt: How do you say "she is short" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: वह refers to "she" here → feminine adjective छोटी.

steps.title: Check · position
steps.prompt: Where do adjectives usually go in Hindi?
steps.explanation: Hindi adjectives precede the noun: एक सुंदर शहर (a beautiful city).

title: Saying no
description: Turn any sentence negative with simple patterns.

steps.title: Negation patterns
steps.body: Each language has a characteristic way to negate a verb. Learn the pattern, apply it everywhere.

steps.title: Patterns compared
steps.body: Position of the negative word differs.
bullets: Portuguese: não before the verb
Arabic: لا (present), لم + jussive (past), ليس (to be)
Hindi: नहीं after the predicate; मत for commands

steps.prompt: Match each Hindi word with its English meaning:
Arrange the stones to say: "I don't like coffee.":
steps.explanation: The negation pattern in its simplest form — learn it once, use it everywhere.

steps.title: Listen · नहीं
steps.prompt: Which is the correct negative form?
Say no, you don't like coffee:
steps.explanation: Hindi negation places नहीं after the verb/adjective: पसंद नहीं.

steps.title: Check · placement
steps.prompt: Where does नहीं typically go in a Hindi sentence?
steps.explanation: नहीं comes after the predicate (adjective, noun, or verb) it negates: पसंद नहीं, है नहीं.

steps.title: Check · command
steps.prompt: Which word is used to negate a command in Hindi?
steps.explanation: मत is used for negative commands: मत जाओ (Don't go!), while नहीं is for statements.

title: Asking questions
description: Question words and patterns.

steps.title: Asking around
steps.body: Each language has its own set of question words and question-formation patterns.

steps.title: Patterns compared
steps.body: Yes/no and information questions each have their own structure.
bullets: Portuguese: rise in intonation + ? punctuation. Or verb-subject inversion.
Arabic: question word + normal word order. هل at start for yes/no.
Hindi: क्या at the start for yes/no; question words stay in the position of what they ask.

steps.prompt: Match each Hindi word with its English meaning:
Arrange the stones to say: "Do you speak English?":
steps.explanation: A well-formed question using the key structure — polite, clear, and natural.

steps.title: Listen · why
steps.prompt: How do you say "why" in Hindi?
Ask where she lives:
steps.explanation: कहाँ रहती हो uses the feminine form रहती for addressing Shreya.

steps.title: Check · word meaning
steps.prompt: How do you say "why" in Hindi?
steps.explanation: क्यों = why; it pairs with क्योंकि (because) in the answer.

steps.title: Check · yes/no question
steps.prompt: Which word is placed at the start to form a yes/no question in Hindi?
steps.explanation: क्या at the start of a statement turns it into a yes/no question: क्या आप बोलते हैं?
